items.title: Hospital industry sues to block HHS' 340B rebate pilot (again)
items.summary: The American Hospital Association and others have launched a legal rematch with the federal government over the second iteration of a pilot program swapping out safety-net hospitals’ upfront drug discounts for after-the-fact rebates.

items.title: BMS fills out Zenbexus picture with post-approval PFS victory in multiple myeloma
items.summary: BMS has put up the progression-free survival numbers on its recently approved Zenbexus regimen, more than doubling the score over a control cocktail of daratumumab, bortezomib and dexamethasone.

items.title: Pfizer's Tukysa snags first-line approval in HER2+ breast cancer maintenance
items.summary: Pfizer bagged a coveted first-line maintenance approval for Tukysa. In combination with HER2 antibody drugs, the treatment can significantly delay disease progression for patients with advanced breast cancer.

items.title: Theramex pays up to $250M for Asieris' novel cervical lesion treatment
items.summary: Should an EU approval go through, the deal allows Asieris to piggyback its global expansion on Theramex’s established women’s health infrastructure across Europe.

items.title: Novartis' Rhapsido tackles 2 most common forms of chronic hives with swift FDA expansion
items.summary: A little over a year after landing its flagship approval in chronic hives, Novartis’ oral BTK inhibitor Rhapsido is expanding its reach with a new FDA nod that comes with a notable ‘first’ for the field.

items.title: Clinical trial applications advice pilot becomes permanent
items.summary: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot, which helps sponsors prepare clinical trial applications, will become a permanent initiative from January 2027…

items.title: Chutes & Ladders—Vir looks to Liu to lead late-stage push
items.summary: As Vir pushes its lead hepatitis D combo through phase 3 development, the biotech has tapped an experienced medical expert to light the way. David Liu, M.D., Ph.D., is now Vir’s chief medical officer, after most recently serving in the same role at Nuvation Bio.

items.title: Ono pays $80M for regional rights to trio of Biohaven IgG degraders, including phase 3 Grave’s asset
items.summary: Japan’s Ono Pharmaceutical is paying $80 million upfront for the regional rights to a trio of Biohaven’s IgG degraders, led by a phase 3-stage Grave’s disease prospect.

items.title: Argenx digests phase 2 celiac win for $2.2B drug, preps pivotal run
items.summary: A phase 2 celiac disease trial of argenx’s FB102 has hit its primary endpoint, delivering a boost to a drug candidate that the biotech acquired in its $2.2 billion takeover of Forte Biosciences.

items.title: Cadrenal launches strategic review for late-stage cardiology pipeline
items.summary: Cadrenal Therapeutics, a heart-focused biotech that recently reached an agreement with the FDA on the design of a pivotal trial for its lead candidate, is now instead looking to offload its pipeline or potentially the entire company.

items.title: Cerevance rescues its Parkinson's drug with phase 3 win
items.summary: Cerevance's oral non-dopaminergic therapy has redeemed itself by improving both motor and non-motor symptoms in a phase 3 Parkinson's disease study.

items.title: Regulatory tracker: FDA clears Tecentriq in colon cancer; Ixchiq axed in UK
items.summary: In this tracker, Fierce Pharma is recording the regulatory progress of in-market products, including expansions into key geographies and new indications. Some of these updates may not meet the bar for standalone stories, but we think they are still worth mentioning.

items.title: FDA’s Rasonque review documents pressure RevMed as investors jitter over KRAS subgroup data
items.summary: Revolution Medicines’ stock slid Thursday after newly released FDA review documents sparked investor unease around Rasonque’s market position in a key KRAS subgroup.

items.title: Teva debuts Weltruza in schizophrenia as much-hyped FDA nod for long-acting olanzapine arrives
items.summary: With a Friday go-ahead from the FDA, another key piece of Teva’s innovation revamp strategy has fallen into place, further bolstering the drugmaker’s footing in schizophrenia.

items.title: Quince relaunches as IRulya, going all in on lung disease after Hail Mary merger
items.summary: To close the book on a tumultuous year, San Francisco's Quince will now operate under the name IRulya Therapeutics, becoming laser-focused on advancing LAM-001, an investigational inhaled formulation of rapamycin being tested in multiple pulmonary diseases.

items.title: Fierce Pharma Asia—Novartis’ $7.8B mRNA deal; Shionogi’s $2B buy; ArriVent’s phase 3 flop
items.summary: Novartis bought an mRNA-coded autoimmune T-cell engager candidate for up to $7.8 billion, as Shionogi offered $2 billion to acquire rare disease drugmaker IntraBio. ArriVent's EGFR inhibitor flunked a first-line phase 3 test in lung cancer. And more.

items.title: Viatris to snap up Pacira's non-opioid pain pipeline for $1.65B
items.summary: In a push to up its investments in patent-protected medicines, Viatris is set to acquire Pacira BioSciences, including two high-margin non-opioid pain therapies.

items.title: Atsena’s Lighthouse gene therapy readout illuminates eye disease efficacy
items.summary: Atsena Therapeutics has reported evidence of efficacy in a clinical trial of an eye disease gene therapy, encouraging the biotech to forge ahead with a study that could support a filing for approval in 2028.

items.title: MimiVax’s cancer vaccine fails phase 2 glioblastoma study, but CEO still sees data as ‘inspiring’
items.summary: MimiVax has reports a phase 2b miss in newly diagnosed glioblastoma patients, but remains positive about a significant survival benefit in a subset of patients 65 years and under.

items.title: Parkinson’s-focused Aspen and bispecific biotech Bambusa plan IPOs
items.summary: Parkinson’s disease cell therapy-focused Aspen Neuroscience and bispecific biotech Bambusa Therapeutics are the latest drug developers to eye up a public listing.

items.title: Ferass Abuzaina named Worldwide President of Surgery at BD
items.summary: Becton, Dickinson and Company has named Ferass Abuzaina as its new Worldwide President of its Surgery business unit.

items.title: GSK drinks in Chai Discovery’s AI models after wet-lab validation
items.summary: GSK has joined Chai Discovery’s growing roster of Big Pharma clients, signing up to access protein-folding and design models.

items.title: ‘We’re making a lot of progress’: How Nobel-winning optogenetics is being harnessed by biotechs
items.summary: As a notorious night owl, it was already very early in the morning of October 5 when Karl Deisseroth, M.D., Ph.D., finally laid down to get some shuteye. Not long after, the phone of the Stanford psychiatrist and bioengineer lit up with an incoming call from Sweden.

items.title: How we picked the Fierce 15
items.summary: What does it mean to be a Fierce 15 biotech in 2026? With this year’s list unveiled, the Fierce Biotech team gets together to discuss what the winners tell us about the state of the sector.

items.title: Lilly-backed TRex rakes in $117M IPO, while hypertension biotech Retension reveals $45M listing
items.summary: Eli Lilly-backed TRex Bio and hypertension-focused Retension Pharmaceuticals brought in $116.7 million and $45 million from their respective IPOs, continuing a bumper year for biotech listings.

items.title: Endeavor’s threat to IPF incumbents increases after phase 2 win for Hedgehog inhibitor
items.summary: Endeavor BioMedicines solidified its potential threat to Big Pharma with a phase 2b readout suggesting its Hedgehog inhibitor could become the first drug to reduce lung fibrosis while increasing total lung capacity.

items.title: AI biotech Iambic aims for $135M IPO to push cancer drugs through clinic
items.summary: Iambic Therapeutics is aiming to raise $135 million in net proceeds from an IPO as the AI biotech looks to fund the clinical development of its lead cancer drug.

items.title: ‘It’s just survival now’: Why is almost a third of Boston’s life sciences lab space sitting vacant?
items.summary: Vacancy rates for lab and manufacturing spaces in Massachusetts increased 11-fold to 31% between 2021 and 2026. So what's gone wrong?

items.title: Zealand, Roche’s ‘intriguing’ weight loss for amylin drug soured by blood sugar data
items.summary: Zealand Pharma has reported more phase 2 data on its Roche-partnered amylin analog, linking the drug candidate to competitive weight loss but a lackluster effect on blood sugar.

items.title: Fierce Biotech Layoff Tracker 2026: Caribou cuts staff, halts pipeline; Foghorn reduces workforce by 40%
items.summary: As always, if you know of layoffs occurring at a biotech, please reach out to the Fierce Biotech editorial team.

items.title: ARPA-H unveils Surpass program to accelerate and expand clinical trials
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services announced the launch of a new program aimed at removing barriers that slow clinical development and transforming how clinical trials are designed and conducted.
